ratings_why.fun: Hold in the back pools or step forward to spawn is a real choice every turn, and the mid-game growth (Bailiff, Hen, Bend-Wife) has a shape I want to climb with; Tiers 1-2 are thin.
ratings_why.distinct: Earn Stamps in the safe back row, then step forward to cash in, pass stats to a neighbour and come back as a Fry: no current tribe plays like that, though Stamps are close to Hedgerow clocks.

verdict_why: v2 closed the endless chains and the unclear texts; what's left is balance the owner tunes, not a fix.

points.text: Early turns are thin: Brother Grilse goes home after one survived attack and leaves a 1/1 Fry. Thumbprint Parr could gain a Stamp when played so Tier 1 shows the passport from turn 1.
With the Bailiff stamping everyone equally, Reunion Secretary is always on. Paying only the largest year-class would make holding counts equal a real choice.

In the hoard build, Llyn Llyw's Attack is the board's Stamp total times units, and that total only climbs. That's the right capstone feel; if it runs too hot, count only back-row Stamps rather than cut the number.
Say whether Mother Redd's spawn count carries over to the fresh copy her Fry becomes, or to an Old Kelt copy; I'd say it resets.

standouts.why: The Bailiff of the Weir is the Tier 3 card that names the comp, and the eating gives it a positional cost.
Old Bradán next to Little Jack Gravel is the payoff the spawning cycle is built to reach, and he resets instead of dying.
Grandfather Under the Alders makes the cash-out turn a planned spike: hold a 12-Stamp fish, then step it forward.

weakest.why: Brother Grilse goes home almost at once, so he gives up his body for +1/+1 when you most need fight wins.
Fish-Pass Keeper is a 3/6 with only a speed effect at Tier 4, where the guide wants buffs or a multiplier.
Passport Seller is mostly a cross-tribe trick; inside the Run it is a Tier 3 body with a weaker Home.

flags.note: Stamps never clear in the hoard build, so the buff grows with Stamps times units; golden Llyn Llyw plus golden Bailiff gives hundreds of Attack by the late game.
Captain Kype reads the same uncapped Stamp total, so in the hoard build he runs as hot as Llyn Llyw.
Old Kelt gives a free copy every turn, which makes triples very fast, including on passported units.
Pilgrim Guide gold repeated by Old Bradán and a golden Little Jack Gravel can pay 12+ gold every few turns.
